title: Next.js Project Setup Handbook
summary: Quick revision notes on scaffolding a Next.js app with create-next-app, the App Router directory layout, next.config, TypeScript and typed routes, path aliases, ESLint, and environment variable files with the NEXT_PUBLIC_ prefix.

chapters.title: Next.js Project Setup Overview
points: create-next-app is the official scaffolder: it generates a project with package.json, config files and a starter app/ directory, then installs dependencies
A Next.js project is driven by four layers: app/ (routes and UI), next.config (framework behaviour), tsconfig.json (types and aliases), .env* files (runtime values)
Mental model: the folder structure under app/ IS the routing table, and config files only tune how that structure is built and served
Scripts in package.json: dev (hot-reload server), build (production build), start (serve the build), lint (run ESLint)

Interview Point: What does create-next-app generate, and which file controls routing versus build behaviour? Why does the folder layout define routes? What is the difference between dev, build and start?

chapters.title: Running create-next-app
points: Run npx create-next-app@latest my-app to start; with no name or flags it prompts interactively
Prompts and flags cover TypeScript, ESLint, Tailwind CSS, src/ directory, App Router and the import alias (default @/*)
Skip the prompts with flags: --ts or --js, --eslint, --tailwind, --src-dir, --app, --import-alias "@/*", and --use-npm, --use-pnpm, --use-yarn or --use-bun
Choosing a package manager flag matters: it decides which lockfile is created and how dependencies are installed
Run the new project with cd my-app && npm run dev; it serves on http://localhost:3000 by default
Common mistake: project names must be lowercase and npm-safe, and running the command inside a non-empty folder with conflicting files fails or overwrites

Interview Point: What does npx create-next-app@latest do, and how do you scaffold non-interactively? What does choosing the src/ directory option change? Which port does the dev server use and how do you change it with -p?

chapters.title: App Directory Structure
points: app/ is the App Router root: each folder is a URL segment, and a route becomes public only when it contains page.tsx or route.ts
Special files: layout.tsx (shared shell that persists), page.tsx (route UI), loading.tsx (Suspense fallback), error.tsx (error boundary, must be a Client Component), not-found.tsx (404 UI)
public/ serves static files from the site root, so public/logo.png is reachable at /logo.png
The optional src/ folder holds app/ and other source code, keeping config files at the project root separate from application code
Organisation tools: (group) folders do not appear in the URL, _private folders opt out of routing, [slug] makes a dynamic segment
Mistake: the root app/layout.tsx is required and must render <html> and <body>; a folder without page.tsx returns 404 even if it holds components
Interview Point: Which files make an app/ folder a public route? How do route groups and private folders differ from normal folders? Why is a root layout mandatory and what must it render?

chapters.title: next.config, TypeScript and Path Aliases
points: next.config.ts (or .js/.mjs) sits at the project root and exports a config object typed as NextConfig; it is read at server start, so changes need a dev server restart

Common options: images.remotePatterns (allow external image hosts), redirects() and rewrites() (async functions returning arrays), output: 'standalone' (self-contained Docker build), env and reactStrictMode
tsconfig.json is generated with strict: true and a Next.js plugin; next-env.d.ts is auto-generated, should not be edited and should stay in .gitignore
Typed routes: set typedRoutes: true in next.config to generate route types so Link href and router.push reject paths that do not exist
Path aliases: compilerOptions.paths { "@/*": ["./src/*"] } (with baseUrl or relative mapping) lets you write import { Button } from '@/components/Button' instead of ../../..
Mistake: changing paths in tsconfig without matching the real folder layout breaks imports, and editing next.config without restarting makes it look like the change did nothing
Interview Point: How does next.config.ts differ from tsconfig.json in responsibility? What does typedRoutes protect you from? How do you configure the @/* alias and why use it over relative imports?

chapters.title: ESLint and Environment Variables
points: ESLint is configured via eslint.config.mjs (flat config) that extends next/core-web-vitals, adding Next.js rules such as no-img-element and no-html-link-for-pages; run it with npm run lint
Add next/typescript to the extends list for TypeScript rules, and lint runs on app, pages, components and src by default
Env files by purpose: .env (all environments), .env.local (local secrets, git-ignored), .env.development and .env.production (per mode), .env.test (tests only)
Load order, highest priority first: process environment, .env.$(NODE_ENV).local, .env.local (skipped in test), .env.$(NODE_ENV), .env
Variables without a prefix stay on the server; only NEXT_PUBLIC_ variables are inlined into the browser bundle at build time, so changing them requires a rebuild

Mistakes: putting secrets in a NEXT_PUBLIC_ variable exposes them to every visitor, committing .env.local leaks credentials, and reading process.env[name] dynamically in client code does not get inlined
Interview Point: What is the difference between a plain env variable and a NEXT_PUBLIC_ one? Which env file wins when the same key is in several? Why must NEXT_PUBLIC_ values be set before build?

chapters.title: Setup Cheat Sheet
points: Scaffold: npx create-next-app@latest my-app, then npm run dev (3000), npm run build, npm run start, npm run lint
Layout: app/ routes, public/ static, src/ optional, root layout.tsx required, page.tsx makes a route public
Special files: layout, page, loading, error, not-found; (group) hidden from URL, _private not routed, [slug] dynamic
Config: next.config.ts (NextConfig, restart on change), typedRoutes: true, images.remotePatterns, output: 'standalone'
TypeScript: tsconfig paths "@/*": ["./src/*"], never edit next-env.d.ts

Env priority: process env > .env.$(NODE_ENV).local > .env.local > .env.$(NODE_ENV) > .env; only NEXT_PUBLIC_ reaches the browser bundle, inlined at build time; a plain variable read in a Client Component still renders into the server HTML during SSR, so read secrets only in server code
Never put secrets in NEXT_PUBLIC_ or commit .env.local; ESLint: eslint.config.mjs extends next/core-web-vitals
